thread:
Aisha (People Ops): Quick Q — downtown office was closed for two weeks last month due to a water main issue. Some folks never badged but were paid remotely or took leave. Does that change PTO accruals/cutoffs for Q2? @Jon (Payroll) any guidance? cc @Lena (HRBP)

Jon (Payroll): Short answer: accruals are based on paid status/pay period, not badge activity. But if there were pay adjustments or unpaid LOAs recorded, that can affect accrual. I'll pull the ledger and confirm by EOD. Can you DM me the list of people you think might be affected?

Megan (People Ops): Also — do we classify the closure as company-paid closure (everyone paid) or optional remote work / leave? That changes how we treat accruals in the system.

Aisha (People Ops): It was a company-closed office; people could work remotely. A few folks logged leave (sick/vacation) in that window. I can export the attendance flags.

Carlos (Eng Manager): For my team most worked remotely and logged normal hours. One contractor took a week off — contractors don't get PTO accrual right?

Jon (Payroll): Correct, contractors per SOW don't accrue PTO. For FTEs: if they were paid for the pay period (no unpaid LOA), accrual should have applied. I'll run a query to be safe: `SELECT emp_id, pay_period, pay_status FROM payroll_ledger WHERE pay_period BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-15';`

Lena (HRBP): If accruals were missed for any paid employees, we should do manual retro adjustments rather than changing policy. Also recommend offering a small carryover exception if someone lost planned leave because of the closure.

Aisha (People Ops): Thanks. @Jon can you confirm numbers and flag any FTEs where accrual wasn't applied? We need retro adjustments before the next payroll cutoff (tomorrow 5pm PT).

Jon (Payroll): On it. Will compile a spreadsheet (emp, period, expected_accrual, actual_accrual, reason). ETA ~2 hours. I'll drop the file in #people-ops-shared and ping here.

Megan (People Ops): I'll draft a short note for impacted employees — keep tone: transparent + what we’re doing to fix.

Carlos (Eng Manager): Appreciate the quick turnaround. For future, can payroll/HR add an "office closure" flag so accruals and communications are automatic? Cuts down tickets.

Lena (HRBP): Good idea. I'll add a line item to the policy FAQ and follow up with the Product (policy) doc updates after we close this.

hr-bot: Reminder: PTO policy v2.1 — accruals are calculated on active paid status per pay period. See https://redwood.internal/hr/pto-policy (internal).

Aisha (People Ops): Great — thanks everyone. I'll update once the spreadsheet is live. If anyone on this thread hears from an impacted employee, please ask them to hold until we confirm numbers.

Jon (Payroll): Spreadsheet uploaded to #people-ops-shared: `office-closure-accruals-2543216789.xlsx` — flagged 7 FTE rows that need manual retro. Will coordinate journal entries with finance.

Megan (People Ops): Thanks @Jon. I'll queue the employee emails and set a short notice explaining retro adjustments (no action required from employees).

Carlos (Eng Manager): Perfect. Appreciate the fast handling. :thumbsup:

Aisha (People Ops): Closing this thread — follow-ups in the shared doc.
